favorable_conditions: Temperature 25-28°C, relative humidity >90%, prolonged leaf wetness, excessive nitrogen, upland/rainfed conditions
economic_impact: Can cause 70-80% yield loss in severe epidemics. Major constraint in all rice-growing regions of India.
symptoms: Diamond/spindle-shaped lesions on leaves with grey center and brown margin
Lesions 1-1.5 cm long, may coalesce to kill entire leaf
Node blast: black lesion at nodes causing stem breakage
Neck blast: grey-brown lesion at panicle base — most destructive form
White panicles (chaffy grains) when neck blast occurs early

treatment.chemical: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP (Beam) at 0.6g/L water or Isoprothiolane 40% EC at 1.5ml/L. First spray at disease appearance, repeat at 10-15 day intervals. Dosage: 300g/acre for Tricyclazole.
treatment.biological: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens at 5g/L water as prophylactic spray at tillering and booting stage.
treatment.cultural: Avoid excessive nitrogen (limit to 100-120 kg/ha). Maintain 2-3 cm standing water. Use balanced NPK (120:60:40 kg/ha). Split nitrogen application.
treatment.dosage: 0.6g per liter of water, 300g per acre

source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research, Hyderabad; PAU Ludhiana Package of Practices

favorable_conditions: Nutrient-deficient soils (especially potassium/silicon), temperature 25-30°C, high humidity, stressed plants
economic_impact: 10-40% yield loss. Historical: caused the Great Bengal Famine of 1943-44. Indicator of poor soil health.
symptoms: Oval/round brown spots on leaves (0.5-1.5 cm) with grey center
Dark brown margin around each lesion is characteristic
Spots also appear on leaf sheath, panicle branches, and glumes
Infected seeds show brown/black discoloration
Severely affected fields appear scorched from distance

treatment.chemical: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP (Dithane M-45) at 2.5g/L water or Zineb 75% WP at 2g/L. Spray at first symptom appearance.
treatment.biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride at 4g/kg seed before sowing.
treatment.cultural: Apply balanced fertilizers — especially potassium (60 kg K2O/ha). Soil testing before season. Use well-decomposed FYM at 10 tonnes/ha.

source: ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad; Directorate of Rice Research

favorable_conditions: Temperature 26-34°C, heavy rainfall, wounds from storms/insects, excessive nitrogen, poor drainage, clipping seedling tips during transplanting
economic_impact: 20-50% yield loss at kresek (wilt) phase. Most destructive bacterial disease of rice worldwide.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions at leaf margins that elongate along veins
Lesions turn yellow, then white/grey, finally brown/grey
Bacterial ooze (milky drops) visible on young lesions in morning
Kresek phase: entire seedlings wilt and die 1-3 weeks after transplanting
Leaves dry from tip downward, often from one side

treatment.chemical: Spray Streptocycline at 0.5g + Copper Oxychloride 50% WP at 2.5g per liter water. Repeat at 7-10 day intervals. Drain fields for 3-4 days before spraying.
treatment.biological: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens at 5g/L water as foliar spray.
treatment.cultural: Reduce nitrogen to 80-100 kg/ha. Ensure proper field drainage. Avoid clipping seedling tips while transplanting. Remove weed hosts.

favorable_conditions: High nitrogen, dense planting, warm temperatures (28-32°C), high humidity, continuous rice cropping
economic_impact: 15-30% yield loss. Second most important fungal disease of rice after blast.
symptoms: Oval/irregular greenish-grey lesions on leaf sheaths near water line
Lesions enlarge and coalesce, developing grey-white center with brown border
Sclerotia (dark brown fungal balls) form on lesion surface
Disease progresses upward from lower sheaths to flag leaf
Panicle infection causes unfilled grains

treatment.chemical: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC at 2ml/L water or Validamycin 3% SL at 2ml/L. Spray at disease appearance, direct spray to lower leaf sheaths.
treatment.biological: Apply Trichoderma harzianum at 5g/L water to lower canopy.
treatment.cultural: Avoid excessive nitrogen. Maintain proper spacing (20×15 cm). Drain excess water. Remove sclerotia from field.
treatment.dosage: 2ml per liter of water, 400ml per acre

resistant_varieties: No highly resistant variety; Tetep, ARC 6650 show moderate resistance
source: ICAR-IIRR; National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack
